Run in CI headless and confirm logs are archived under logs/ci/**.

title: Integrate GdUnit4 suites into quality_gates.py
description: Extend scripts/python/quality_gates.py to optionally run selected GdUnit4 suites (adapters/security as hard gate, integration/UI as soft gate) and aggregate results into a single summary JSON. Source: docs/migration/Phase-13-Quality-Gates-Backlog.md (B2).
acceptance: 在 Windows 环境运行 quality_gates.py 且启用 GdUnit4 参数时，必须在同次执行记录中看到被选 suite 的执行结果与门禁类型；未启用该参数时，必须将对应 suite 明确标记为未运行，并写入 logs/ci/<date>/task-0054.json。 Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_quality_gates_gdunit_suite_wiring.gd

在 Windows/PowerShell 下，quality_gates.py 必须能解析并实际执行 GdUnit4 相关参数；脚本退出码必须与总体门禁结论一致（通过=0，失败=非0），并将结果写入 logs/ci/<date>/task-0054.json。 Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_quality_gates_gdunit_suite_wiring.gd
Overlay 文档的 Test-Refs 必须覆盖与 GdUnit4 接线相关的验证项，且每一项都能回链到本任务描述或测试策略，避免引入与本任务无关的引用。 Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_quality_gates_gdunit_suite_wiring.gd

quality_gates.py 必须提供参数以显式选择是否运行 GdUnit4 suites，并在结果中区分 adapters/security 与 integration/UI 两类 suites。 Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task54GdUnitGatePolicyTests.cs Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_quality_gates_gdunit_suite_wiring.gd
adapters/security suites 任一失败必须导致总体门禁失败；integration/UI suites 失败仅记录为软门禁，不阻断总体通过。 Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task54QualityGateSummaryTests.cs
执行后必须生成单一机器可读 summary JSON，包含各 suite 状态、门禁级别与总体门禁结论，并输出到 logs/ci/<date>/quality-gates/summary.json。 Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_gdunit_junit_artifact_export.gd

GdUnit4 的 JUnit/XML 输出必须写入 logs/e2e/<date>/gdunit/junit.xml；若未生成该文件，summary 必须明确记录未生成原因。 Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task54CiDecisionSyncTests.cs Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_quality_gates_gdunit_suite_wiring.gd

本地分别在开启与关闭 GdUnit4 参数运行 quality_gates.py 时，summary 中 suites 状态必须可区分为已运行与未运行，不能以缺失字段代替。 Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task54GdUnitSuiteSelectionTests.cs Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_quality_gates_gdunit_suite_wiring.gd
CI 任务必须以 summary JSON 的总体门禁结论作为 pass/fail 判定依据，且结论变化时 CI 结果同步变化。 Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task54CiDecisionSyncTests.cs
Test-Refs 列表必须包含 logs/ci/<date>/quality-gates/summary.json 与 logs/e2e/<date>/gdunit/junit.xml，且路径与实际产物一致。 Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task54GdUnitGatePolicyTests.cs

Test-Refs 列表必须包含 Tests.Godot/tests/ci/test_gdunit_suite_wiring.gd 与 Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task32AcceptanceTests.cs，并可对应到本任务验收项。 Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task54CiDecisionSyncTests.cs Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_quality_gates_gdunit_suite_wiring.gd
在 ACCEPTANCE_CHECKLIST.md 中必须明确列出 ADR-0005、ADR-0011、ADR-0024 作为本任务门禁语义口径引用。 Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task54QualityGateSummaryTests.cs
test_strategy: Run quality_gates.py locally with and without GdUnit4 flags to verify behavior.
Validate CI job consumes the summary JSON for pass/fail decisions.

title: Coverage thresholds as configurable soft/hard gate
description: Align xUnit coverage thresholds to the blueprint target (lines >= 90%, branches >= 85%) and allow overriding via environment variables. Provide soft/hard gate modes in scripts/python/run_dotnet.py and scripts/python/quality_gates.py.
acceptance: In scripts/python/run_dotnet.py and scripts/python/quality_gates.py, default coverage thresholds are lines>=90 and branches>=85, and those defaults must be used when no override environment variables are provided. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task55CoverageScriptEntrypointBindingTests.cs

Coverage threshold environment overrides must be resolved and applied in both scripts, and each script must evaluate gates using its effective thresholds so non-default threshold runs are achievable without code changes. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task55CoverageScriptEntrypointBindingTests.cs

Both scripts must expose semantically consistent soft/hard gate behavior: for identical measured coverage below effective thresholds, soft returns exit code 0 with warning and hard returns non-zero; when measured coverage meets or exceeds effective thresholds, both return 0. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task55CoverageScriptEntrypointBindingTests.cs

A single machine-readable coverage summary contract must be used for CI outputs; emitted summaries at logs/unit/<date>/summary.json and logs/ci/<date>/quality-gates/summary.json must both include measured line/branch coverage, effective thresholds (after env overrides), gate mode, and pass/fail with identical field semantics. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task55CoverageScriptEntrypointBindingTests.cs

For the same environment overrides, run_dotnet.py and quality_gates.py must resolve equivalent effective threshold values (lines/branches) before gate evaluation. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task55CoverageScriptEntrypointBindingTests.cs

Gate-mode selection semantics must remain consistent between run_dotnet.py and quality_gates.py for identical measured/effective coverage inputs. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task55CoverageScriptEntrypointBindingTests.cs
test_strategy: Run dotnet tests on Windows and verify threshold behavior by temporarily setting env vars.

title: Audit JSONL validation + gate integration
description: Add a Python validator for security audit JSONL outputs and integrate it into the quality gates flow.
acceptance: Provide scripts/python/validate_audit_logs.py that validates security-audit JSONL line by line for JSON structure and required fields; any invalid line must cause a non-zero exit and the validation result must not be reported as passed. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0056AcceptanceTests.cs

When validation fails, the output must include the exact failing line number and an actionable fix reason so the broken row can be repaired directly. Refs: Tests/CI/AuditLogs/ValidateAuditLogsTests.cs

When audit validation is enabled, quality_gates.py must invoke the audit validator and persist the actual executed/pass_fail result into the task-0056 summary JSON. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0056AcceptanceTests.cs

If audit validation is enabled and validate_audit_logs.py fails, quality_gates.py must persist task-0056 summary with audit_validation.executed=true and pass_fail="fail" before exiting non-zero to block downstream release flow. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0056AcceptanceTests.cs, Tests/CI/AuditLogs/ValidateAuditLogsTests.cs
Provide valid and invalid JSONL fixtures and reproduce one passing run and one failing run on Windows. Refs: Tests/CI/AuditLogs/ValidateAuditLogsTests.cs

When audit validation is disabled, quality_gates.py must not invoke validate_audit_logs.py and must write executed=false and pass_fail="skipped" into task-0056 summary. Refs: Tests/CI/AuditLogs/ValidateAuditLogsTests.cs
test_strategy: Use valid/invalid JSONL fixtures to reproduce one pass and one fail run on Windows.

title: Traceability gate for ADR/Chapter/Overlay links
description: Split from T56: enforce ADR, chapter, and overlay Test-Refs traceability as a dedicated gate task.
acceptance: task-0057-traceability.json must record pass/fail results for ADR-0019, ADR-0003, and ADR-0005 trace checks. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task57TraceabilityGateTests.cs
task-0057-traceability.json must record pass/fail results for chapter trace checks CH02, CH03, and CH07. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task57TraceabilityGateTests.cs
Overlay files _index.md, 08-Feature-Slice-M1-Warrior.md, and ACCEPTANCE_CHECKLIST.md must all contain searchable T56/T57 Test-Refs entries. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task57TraceabilityGateTests.cs
Any ADR/chapter/overlay trace mismatch must fail the traceability gate with non-zero exit and block downstream release steps. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task57TraceabilityGateTests.cs
Traceability output must include machine-readable missing/mismatch diff items with concrete file/key locations. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task57TraceabilityGateTests.cs
Traceability check must run on Windows and output platform=windows in task-0057-traceability.json. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task57TraceabilityGateTests.cs

On Windows, the traceability check test strategy must run one pass sample and one fail sample: the pass sample exits 0 with no mismatch diff entries, and the fail sample exits non-zero with mismatch diff entries. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task57TraceabilityGateTests.cs

Task57TraceabilityGateTests.cs must cover ADR/chapter/overlay checks and assertions must match task-0057-traceability.json pass/fail and diff output. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task57TraceabilityGateTests.cs

Traceability gate must run as a dedicated CI job or dedicated command; if this gate is skipped, unrecognized, or not executed, pipeline must fail before release stages. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task57TraceabilityGateTests.cs

Gate must explicitly validate consistency across tasks.json ADR/chapter refs and overlay Test-Refs anchors (bidirectional): missing or mismatched links in either direction must fail with non-zero exit. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task57TraceabilityGateTests.cs

Traceability gate must validate full linkage consistency among task adr_refs/chapter_refs/overlay_refs and overlay 08 Test-Refs anchors (_index.md, 08-Feature-Slice-M1-Warrior.md, ACCEPTANCE_CHECKLIST.md); any missing, stale, or mismatched link must fail with non-zero exit and emit machine-readable diffs. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task57TraceabilityGateTests.cs

Validator must parse and compare these exact fields for Task 57: tasks.json master.adrRefs/chapterRefs/overlay, tasks_back.json and tasks_gameplay.json adr_refs/chapter_refs/overlay_refs, and overlay 08 Test-Refs entries; the consistency scope must include ADR refs, chapter refs, overlay refs, and Test-Refs path anchors. Any mismatch or missing item in this scope must fail gate with non-zero exit and JSON diff evidence. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task57TraceabilityGateTests.cs

必须校验 ADR / 章节 / Overlay Test-Refs 一致性：对比 tasks.json 与 tasks_back.json/tasks_gameplay.json 以及 overlay 文档中的 Test-Refs，任一缺失、错链、过期链接都必须判定失败并输出 diff。 Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task57TraceabilityGateTests.cs

The dedicated validator must compare all required link domains declared by the task metadata against overlay documents, emit JSON diff entries for every missing/stale/mismatched link, and return non-zero when any diff exists. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task57TraceabilityGateTests.cs

Dedicated checker must validate ADR refs, chapter refs, and overlay Test-Refs links across task metadata and overlay documents, emit machine-readable diffs for every missing/stale/mismatched link, and return non-zero when any mismatch exists. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task57TraceabilityGateTests.cs
test_strategy: Run traceability check on Windows with one pass sample and one fail sample.

title: Semantic scope governance for soft review stabilization
description: Create a governance guardrail that keeps semantic soft review bounded to task scope while preserving deterministic hard-gate precedence.
acceptance: task-0058-semantic-governance.json must include semantic_policy_mode, gate_precedence, and governance_result fields with non-empty values. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task58SemanticScopeGovernanceTests.cs

Policy evaluation scope must be limited to task.master.details and task.mapped.acceptance: when master.details is non-empty, task_context.allowed_scope_items must include both; when master.details is empty, task_context.allowed_scope_items must include only "task.mapped.acceptance". Any scope expansion beyond allowed_scope_items must be classified as advisory out-of-scope and must not become blocker without explicit elevation rule. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task58SemanticScopeGovernanceTests.cs

When acceptance_check is ok and llm_review has warn-level findings only (without explicit elevation), governance_result must be pass and advisory notes must be recorded. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task58SemanticScopeGovernanceTests.cs
When acceptance_check fails, governance_result must be fail regardless of llm_review output. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task58SemanticScopeGovernanceTests.cs
Governance output must expose machine-readable blocker_findings and advisory_findings fields using stable key names. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task58SemanticScopeGovernanceTests.cs
Windows execution evidence in task-0058-semantic-governance.json must include platform=windows and a non-empty run_id. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task58SemanticScopeGovernanceTests.cs

One pass sample and one advisory-warning sample must both be reproducible via local scripts without manual file edits, and each generated task-0058-semantic-governance.json must include machine-readable evidence_refs.acceptance_check_summary and evidence_refs.llm_review_summary paths pointing to logs/ci/<date>/sc-acceptance-check-task-<id>/summary.json and logs/ci/<date>/sc-llm-review-task-<id>/summary.json. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task58SemanticScopeGovernanceTests.cs

If any llm_review finding is explicitly elevated to blocker, output must include elevation_rule_id and supporting evidence and the finding must appear in blocker_findings; without an explicit elevation rule, warn findings must remain in advisory_findings and must not fail governance. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task58SemanticScopeGovernanceTests.cs

Given identical acceptance_check, llm_review, and task context inputs, policy evaluation must produce stable governance_result and identical blocker/advisory classification across repeated runs (review oscillation guard). Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task58SemanticScopeGovernanceTests.cs

For both pass sample and advisory-warning sample, generated evidence summaries must include non-empty status, task_id, generated_at, and findings/summary counters. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task58SemanticScopeGovernanceTests.cs
test_strategy: Run governance evaluation on Windows with one pass sample and one advisory-warning sample, then validate JSON evidence shape and linkage fields.

title: Upgrade Map route graph visualization on top of existing route ownership
description: Track the M1 route-graph guardrail as an upgrade on top of the existing route-owned Map flow so visual route connections, legal edge state, and legacy shortcut suppression remain explicit in backlog and quality gates.
acceptance: On M1 Map, the player-facing entry presents a connected route graph with visible legal-transition edges, continues to use the existing route-owned Map-to-node transition flow, does not present the four standalone node-type shortcut buttons as the primary entry path, and does not introduce any parallel Map-to-node transition owner or second execution path. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Map/test_map_tree_route.gd

The M1 route graph must expose a deterministic directed edge set for the full five-floor route: every non-terminal node has at least one legal outgoing edge to the next floor, the final node has no outgoing edge, and no edge skips floors or points to an undefined node ID. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Map/test_map_tree_route.gd

Map rendering makes reachable, locked, completed, and selected-path states visually distinguishable on both nodes and edges so currently legal choices are directly observable. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Map/test_map_tree_route.gd

Selecting a reachable node triggers the existing route-owned Map-to-node transition; selecting a locked or disconnected node shows visible refusal feedback, does not transition, and keeps run progression unchanged. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Map/test_map_tree_route.gd

After node completion, route-graph reachability updates so only legal next-floor nodes and connecting edges become reachable, while traversed segments remain visible as completed path history. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Map/test_map_tree_route.gd

When route-graph entry is active, legacy ActionRow shortcut buttons (Combat, Event, Shop, Rest) are hidden or removed from the player-facing Map. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Map/test_map_tree_route.gd

Route-node selection must have a single execution authority: reachable-node selection resolves exactly once through the existing route-owned transition path, while locked/disconnected selections resolve to refusal feedback only and never invoke an alternative scene transition path. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Map/test_map_tree_route.gd

Workflow-selection gate evidence for T70 must be recorded before implementation evidence is accepted; verification must assert a concrete workflow-selection summary artifact exists with task_id=70 and that its timestamp is not later than the selected implementation evidence timestamp. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0070AcceptanceTests.cs
test_strategy: Extend the existing Map route GdUnit suite to cover connected route graph edges, path-state visualization, legal unlock progression, and hidden legacy shortcut buttons on Windows.

title: Consolidate combat deck lifecycle wiring as the umbrella task for T80-T82
description: Track the combat deck-lifecycle umbrella milestone over T80-T82 so backlog and quality gates treat this work as an integration checkpoint over existing deck/runtime capabilities, not as a separate build track.
acceptance: T80 is accepted only when evidence from the shared DeckService/CardState runtime path shows deterministic combat deck-lifecycle outcomes for draw-pile-to-hand draw, turn-end discard into discard pile, exhaust-pile placement, and discard-to-draw reshuffle ordering. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Services/DeckServiceTests.cs Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

T81 is accepted only when Combat scene/HUD wiring remains synchronized with runtime transitions for draw, hand, discard, and exhaust states, and scene code is limited to binding/orchestration without taking scene-local deck-lifecycle ownership or duplicating lifecycle logic. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Services/DeckServiceTests.cs Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

T82 can close this umbrella milestone only when Windows-run evidence from existing deck-lifecycle and Combat scene suites aggregates T80 and T81 results; introducing a fourth parallel implementation path or standalone duplicate track fails acceptance. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

The aggregated T80-T82 milestone evidence must explicitly verify hand state, exhaust pile, turn-end discard behavior, deterministic ordering, and Windows-backed execution, in addition to draw/discard/reshuffle behavior and HUD synchronization. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Services/DeckServiceTests.cs Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

T71 remains milestone-only: validation must run through existing DeckService and Combat scene suites, and acceptance fails if a replacement verification lane or a fourth implementation path is used. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Services/DeckServiceTests.cs Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

No implementation evidence under this task is valid unless workflow selection of T71 is recorded first, and the review evidence set must include that selection record before implementation evidence. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0071WorkflowSelectionEvidenceTests.cs
test_strategy: Validate this milestone by aggregating T80-T82 evidence from existing DeckService and Combat scene suites; do not add a separate implementation-only test slice under T71.

title: Bind CombatScene to existing data-driven card definitions and localized card text
description: Track CombatScene binding to existing card definitions, translations, and effect contracts so data-driven card behavior does not fork into a second card model.
acceptance: When CombatScene renders playable cards, each card button shows localized card name, cost, card type, and player-visible effect summary sourced from the existing card-definition and translation contracts, with no hard-coded scene text and no parallel card text/model source. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0072AcceptanceTests.cs

Playing any damage, block, status, or mixed-effect card resolves strictly from its existing card definition (including cost payment, targeting rule, and exhaust/discard routing); for each effect component, only definition-allowed targets are mutated and non-target entities remain unchanged, and resulting HP, block, energy, and pile states match that definition. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0072AcceptanceTests.cs

Each successful card play emits visible player-facing feedback that matches the resolved outcomes, including damage dealt, block gained, statuses applied, and whether the card was exhausted or discarded. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_feedback_log.gd Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0072AcceptanceTests.cs

If play is rejected due to insufficient energy, missing card definition, or invalid targeting rule, the UI presents refusal feedback and leaves HP, block, energy, and pile states unchanged. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_feedback_log.gd Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0072AcceptanceTests.cs

On the M1 combat surface, both en and zh-CN must render localized card name and localized card body/effect description for playable cards (including Strike and Defend) from the existing translation + card-definition contracts, with visible cost/type data from the same existing definition path; raw localization keys or placeholder text are not allowed. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_m1_visible_text_flow.gd Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0072AcceptanceTests.cs

CombatScene reads card type from existing card definitions and uses that type for combat presentation and interaction behavior, without hard-coded fallback typing or any parallel card-description path. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0072AcceptanceTests.cs

When a status card is played, the defined status is applied to the correct target, and when an exhaust-effect card is played, that card is moved to exhaust (not discard) per the existing definition path. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_feedback_log.gd Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0072AcceptanceTests.cs

CombatScene card loading uses only existing contracts and current card data files, and does not introduce any new card-definition path or new card-data file family. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0072AcceptanceTests.cs

Legacy hard-coded Strike/Defend UI/effect wiring is removed from CombatScene runtime behavior: rendering, cost display, targeting, and resolution for Strike/Defend must come from the same existing card definition + localization + effect contracts path as all other cards, without card-specific hard-coded branches. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_feedback_log.gd Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0072AcceptanceTests.cs

Before workflow selection evidence marks Task 72 as selected, CombatScene implementation changes for this task must not be executable/claimed as delivered; once selected, implementation evidence must trace to the same existing card-definition + localization + effect-contract path (no parallel model path). Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0072AcceptanceTests.cs

For target-rule edge cases (self-only, enemy-only, and invalid selected target), CombatScene must apply or refuse strictly per existing card targeting contracts, with refusal feedback and unchanged state on invalid selection. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_feedback_log.gd Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0072AcceptanceTests.cs
test_strategy: Extend Combat scene binding and feedback suites to cover data-driven card definitions, localized text, effect summaries, and refusal paths.

title: Upgrade existing combat targeting and victory routing to multi-enemy runtime state
description: Track the upgrade from the current single-target or partial targeting skeleton to route-owned multi-enemy combat state, without replacing existing victory-route ownership.
acceptance: In multi-enemy runtime state, Combat must expose every living legal runtime enemy as a selectable and inspectable target entry, and each exposed enemy must surface name, HP, block, status, and intent. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

Card play must enforce legal targeting: single-target cards resolve only when a living legal enemy is selected, and on success the effect applies to the selected enemy only; non-selected enemies must remain unchanged unless the card explicitly declares all-enemy/global behavior, while self-target and all-enemy cards resolve without selecting an enemy. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Battle/test_battle_card_targeting_drag_play_flow.gd Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

If the selected target is invalid, dead, locked, or disconnected, card play must be rejected with visible feedback, and HP, energy, and pile state must stay unchanged. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Battle/test_battle_card_targeting_drag_play_flow.gd

When an enemy dies, it must be removed from the legal target set, and the remaining enemies must keep deterministic combat state with intent still visible. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

After all enemies are defeated, combat completion must remain route-owned and must transition to Reward or Map based on current node rules. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_m1_visible_text_flow.gd

Combat victory routing must not trigger while any legal living enemy remains; route-owned completion may execute only after the legal living enemy set becomes empty. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_m1_visible_text_flow.gd

If the currently selected enemy becomes dead, disconnected, or otherwise illegal before card resolution, Combat must clear or deterministically retarget selection and must never resolve card effects against an illegal target. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Battle/test_battle_card_targeting_drag_play_flow.gd Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd
test_strategy: Extend Combat and targeting flow suites to cover legal target resolution, invalid target refusal, enemy death, and combat completion routing.

title: Upgrade existing targeting flow with Slay-the-Spire-style card drag UX
description: Track drag targeting as an input-layer upgrade over the current validated play path, while preserving the existing accessibility fallback.
acceptance: Dragging a card from hand onto a legal target and releasing it must issue the play request through the current validated card-play path (the same path used by click-based play). Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/UI/test_card_drag_target_play.gd Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Battle/test_battle_card_targeting_drag_play_flow.gd

While a dragged card is hovering a legal target, the UI shows a visible target highlight/preview, and no combat state change is applied before release. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/UI/test_card_drag_target_play.gd

Dropping on an invalid target or empty area does not commit play: visible invalid/cancel feedback is shown, the card returns to hand, and energy plus pile state remain unchanged. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Battle/test_battle_card_targeting_drag_play_flow.gd

The click path and Play Selected Card accessibility path both remain usable, and a successful legal activation is behaviorally equivalent to a successful legal drag release through the same play flow. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd
Drag preview and target-hover interactions are UI-only and must not advance combat RNG streams or route progression. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/UI/test_card_drag_target_play.gd

Keyboard fallback and controller fallback must each complete target selection and play via the same validated card-play path as drag release, without introducing a separate combat input stack. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

Implementation for this task proceeds only after workflow explicitly selects T74, and review evidence includes that workflow-selection record before implementation evidence. Refs: logs/ci/<date>/single-task-light-lane-v2-batch/shards/shard-001-t70-89/summary.json
test_strategy: Promote existing drag-target harness coverage into real Combat scene behavior tests, including valid drop, invalid drop, cancel, and accessibility fallback.

title: Wire existing status contracts and rules into visible combat status effects
description: Track combat status visibility as wiring of existing status contracts and rule semantics into the player-facing combat runtime, rather than a duplicate status implementation.
acceptance: When player or enemy statuses are active in combat (including strength, weak, vulnerable, block, poison, and temporary modifiers), each active status is shown on the combat surface with a readable label, visible stack/value, and decision-useful tooltip/detail text, and no active status is omitted. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

Given the same initial combat state and action sequence, damage and mitigation results are identical across repeated runs, and contributions from strength, weak, vulnerable, block-like effects, poison ticks, and temporary modifiers come from the existing status/modifier rule path. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

At turn boundaries, status apply/stack/decay/expire changes are reflected in HUD/feedback within the same turn flow, so the current status state is fully readable from UI feedback without log inspection. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_feedback_log.gd

If combat encounters an invalid or expired status reference, the invalid effect is rejected, visible failure feedback is emitted, and combat state remains non-corrupted and playable. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_feedback_log.gd
On M1 combat surfaces, status-related UI text renders correctly in en and zh-CN and never exposes raw localization keys. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

Status rendering, damage/mitigation resolution, and turn-boundary decay all execute through the shared existing status contracts/services path, with no UI-local rule path used for those outcomes. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_feedback_log.gd

UI-only modules do not define parallel status semantics for stacking, decay, or modifier computation; presence of a parallel UI status-rule path fails this task. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

Implementation evidence for T75 is valid only if workflow-selection evidence explicitly selecting T75 appears first; if selection evidence is missing or appears after implementation evidence, acceptance fails. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0075WorkflowSelectionEvidenceTests.cs
test_strategy: Extend Combat UI binding and feedback tests to cover status rendering, status-modified damage/block resolution, and turn-boundary decay.

title: Bind enemy intent generation and preview to data-driven AI on existing intent surfaces
description: Replace fixed enemy attack preview with data-driven intent generation and preview while deferring enemy action resolution and no-repeat guardrails to a follow-up task.
acceptance: Before any player action, the existing intent surface renders enemy intent generated from enemy AI behavior definitions as the single source (no fixed/hardcoded fallback preview), and the rendered intent can express attack, block, buff, debuff, and mixed intent outputs. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

Enemy behavior selection for intent preview uses the named combat RNG stream, while UI-only interactions (hover, drag preview, localization refresh) leave that stream state unchanged; this task covers intent generation/preview only and does not execute enemy action resolution or no-repeat guardrail enforcement. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

With the same deterministic inputs, the upgraded intent path produces repeatable enemy intent output, and this determinism is verifiable without invoking enemy turn execution or action-resolution paths. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

T76 scope is limited to enemy intent generation and preview binding; enemy action resolution and no-repeat guardrail enforcement are explicitly out of scope for T76 acceptance paths. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

The upgrade reuses the existing intent surface nodes and binding points; no parallel replacement intent surface is introduced in this task. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

Under deterministic seed/inputs, enemy intent preview generated from AI behavior definitions remains repeatable and visible on existing intent surfaces, and UI-only operations do not advance the named combat RNG stream. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd
test_strategy: Extend Combat scene tests to cover deterministic enemy intent generation, visible preview, and UI-only RNG non-advancement on the upgraded intent path.

title: Integrate trigger registration and combat-time hooks into the shared combat runtime
description: Integrate deterministic trigger registration and card-play, turn, damage, and death-check hooks into combat runtime while deferring powers/relics/potions presentation and effect integration to a follow-up task.
acceptance: On the shared combat runtime path, trigger registration and execution order is deterministic for card-play, turn-start, turn-end, damage, and death-check hooks; repeated identical runs produce identical hook order and outcomes, and no second trigger stack is used. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

For this task scope, card-play/turn/damage/death-check hooks are integrated into current combat flow so state-changing outcomes are observable through existing combat feedback/history outputs; route-owned completion behavior stays unchanged, and powers/relics/potions presentation or effectful integration is not introduced. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_feedback_log.gd

The shared combat runtime exposes one auditable trigger-registration path, and trigger execution consumes registrations only from that shared path, not from side-channel or duplicate stacks. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

After integrating these hooks, combat completion ownership remains in the route flow; trigger processing must not finalize or redirect route completion on its own. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_feedback_log.gd

Acceptance fails if this task adds powers, relics, or potions presentation/effectful integration; those capabilities remain deferred to follow-up tasks in this phase. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_feedback_log.gd

Implementation evidence for T77 is valid only when a prior workflow-selection record explicitly shows T77 was selected before coding or test evidence appears in the review trail. Refs: logs/ci/<date>/single-task-light-lane-v2-batch/shards/shard-001-t70-89/summary.json
test_strategy: Add deterministic trigger-order assertions through existing Combat scene suites for card-play, turn, damage, and death-check hooks on the shared runtime path.

title: Layer combat presentation feedback on top of deterministic state without mutating runtime logic
description: Track the presentation-feedback layer as a UI-only overlay on existing deterministic combat runtime, without introducing a second logic path.
acceptance: For every successful card play and every resolved enemy action, the presentation layer must emit transient visible feedback (damage numbers, block gain numbers, card-play motion cues, and hit/action feedback) in addition to HUD updates, and deterministic combat outcomes must remain identical to baseline runs. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

When card play, hit, block, invalid action, or enemy action runtime events occur, the corresponding combat SFX hook must be triggered; if an audio asset is missing, action resolution must still complete safely and required visible feedback must still be produced (audio playback may explicitly no-op) without runtime failure. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_feedback_log.gd

Hovering or focusing a card must display a readable preview containing cost, type, target rule, and localized effect text, and opening/closing this preview must not mutate deterministic combat state or advance/consume RNG. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

Hovering or focusing enemy intent must display readable detail for incoming damage, block, or status effects, and showing/hiding this detail must not mutate deterministic turn state or RNG progression. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

In reduced-motion or headless-safe mode, presentation feedback must remain test-observable via deterministic nodes/events/log outputs without depending on wall-clock animation timing, and combat state plus RNG outputs must match deterministic baselines. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_feedback_log.gd

Card-play motion cues and hit feedback must each be independently observable as presentation-layer outputs, not only inferred from static HUD value changes. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_feedback_log.gd

All presentation feedback must be sourced from the existing deterministic combat event path and must not create a second combat logic path or mutate runtime combat state. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

For feedback dispatch on card play, enemy action, hit, block, invalid action, and previews, deterministic combat state and RNG progression must be unchanged before versus after presentation-layer handling. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_feedback_log.gd

Implementation for this task must start only after workflow explicitly selects T78, and review evidence must include that workflow-selection record before any implementation evidence. Refs: logs/ci/<date>/single-task-light-lane-v2-batch/shards/shard-001-t70-89/summary.json
test_strategy: Extend Combat UI tests with observable presentation-layer nodes/events and verify they do not mutate deterministic combat state or RNG.

title: Unify combat defeat trigger by HP change event and single-resolution guard
description: Track defeat routing unification across existing HP mutation paths so any HP<=0 transition resolves exactly once.
acceptance: All existing player-HP mutation entry points (including end-turn and non-end-turn paths) MUST call the same logic-state HP update entry (single-source state-update path); defeat routing MUST trigger only on HP transitions >0 -> <=0 from that unified path, and HP changes that do not cross this boundary (<=0 -> <=0 or >0 -> >0) MUST NOT trigger defeat resolve. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_m1_visible_text_flow.gd

Within one combat resolution, defeat resolve is one-shot: after the first HP transition from >0 to <=0, the observable outcome MUST be Defeat summary + Main menu exactly once; no later HP updates (including recover-above-zero then drop-again, or staying <=0) may trigger another defeat resolve or replace Defeat with Victory. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_m1_visible_text_flow.gd

When HP<=0 triggers defeat, route ownership remains unchanged from current behavior, and the observable outcome is return to Main menu with a visible Defeat summary result. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_m1_visible_text_flow.gd

Each existing player-HP mutation entry point (end-turn and non-end-turn) must be exercised and shown to produce identical HP-change-driven defeat behavior through the same state-update semantics; any entry point that can cause defeat without the unified HP-change flow fails acceptance. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_m1_visible_text_flow.gd

HP-change emission/callback MUST be produced by the unified logic-state update path for every HP mutation update (not defeat-only), with test-visible evidence on both end-turn and non-end-turn entry points; defeat routing MUST be causally bound to that emission when and only when HP transitions >0 -> <=0. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_m1_visible_text_flow.gd

No parallel defeat trigger is allowed outside the unified HP state-update flow: if a code path can resolve defeat without passing through the unified HP-change emission, acceptance fails even when observable routing appears correct. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_m1_visible_text_flow.gd

Implementation evidence for T79 is valid only if workflow selection of T79 is recorded first; if implementation artifacts appear before workflow selection evidence, acceptance is not met. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0079WorkflowSelectionEvidenceTests.cs
test_strategy: Add/extend Combat scene tests for HP-change-driven defeat trigger on end-turn and non-end-turn HP mutation paths, and verify one-shot defeat routing.

title: Wire CombatScene to existing DeckService runtime state instead of local pile counters
